speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment what is the rationale for Singapore being a potential claimant from the Loss and Damage Fund set up in COP27, in view that many other potential claimant countries from this fund have much lower levels of GDP per capita and income than Singapore does.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: I have no update to provide to the House.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The Member may wish to refer to that reply.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: I think in the last exchange, the Minister mentioned that Singapore is currently considering to be either a claimant or a donor to the 2022 United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP27) Biodiversity Fund.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: But maybe I would like to thank the Member for his support for the Loss and Damage Fund and in helping developing countries.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: If I may, Mr Speaker, maybe ask the Member for his position, whether the Workers' Party supports contributing to the fund and if so, what amount should we contribute and to which countries.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Besides the Democratic Republic of the Congo, where would he draw the line between developing countries and least developed countries?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: I think we should make a reasonable contribution.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: And where do you draw the balance point on that?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: I do not have a figure, but I think we can take reference, perhaps from other developed countries with a similar size of economy, of gross domestic product (GDP) as ours and use that as a reference point.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: How should those funds be disbursed to different developing countries?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: I think it should be in proportion to the needs and the resources of those developing countries, meaning to say in proportion to the land area and biodiversity challenge that those developing countries face, and the funding, GDP, availability of government funds that those developing countries have.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: I take it that the Member would recommend that we tag our contribution or donation to the fund at the GDP level, regardless of whether it is a developing or developed country, or whether it is taking into consideration things like population size.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: I would also like to perhaps clarify from the Member whether he would suggest that we move away from the agreement that we have reached in Paris.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Because so far, the Paris Agreement is the basis for all discussions and, in the Paris Agreement, there are certain understandings that have been reached.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Is the Member suggesting that for the Loss and Damage Fund, we should move away from established agreement internationally?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Basically, just to reiterate what I just said, because I am not sure if what the Minister had recapitulated reflected what I said.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: I was suggesting that, in terms of the donation that we make to the COP27 fund, reference can be taken from what other developed countries of a similar size or GDP to ours are donating.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: That means you look at what other developed countries are doing and you normalise that according to GDP.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: And for where those funds should go, that should be distributed according to the challenges that the developing countries are facing in terms of biodiversity scale and the resources that those developing countries have to address the issues.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: This is just to clarify what I said earlier.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Should we move away from the Paris Agreement?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: In fact, I would like to ask the Minister to share whether donating to the COP27 fund necessarily involves deviating from previous agreements made in Paris.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: It is not my understanding that it does, but perhaps she has a different perspective and some information to share on that point.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The Clerk will now proceed to read the Order of the Day.
